title: Every Street Sign Tells Its Own Etymology Story | vitalii.no
description:
Street names carry real history - Kolbuvegen is named after the village of Kolbu, 15 km away - but there was no way to learn that while driving past the sign at 70 km/h. I also didn't want the app guessing at meanings it couldn't actually back up with a source.

I extended the harvester to keep every named street pulled from OpenStreetMap, not just the ones that already had an article, recording each street's road class, length, and the places at both ends. The story prompt opens with the Norwegian phrase for 'you're now driving on,' splits the street name into its component words with their meaning, and only states what a name refers to when a source actually confirms the link - matching Kolbuvegen to the village of Kolbu because the street name starts with the place name. Street-name stories are now ranked ahead of other place stories, and the app matches the car's current street on every GPS fix.

Every named street on my route now has the chance to explain itself in two languages instead of staying an anonymous sign. Road stubs under 60 meters, or names that map to only a single address, are automatically skipped rather than forced into a weak story.
